description: A freshly published version can be a compromised one. Hold every update for 7 days so a hijacked release is yanked before Renovate proposes it. Security updates bypass the hold through vulnerabilityAlerts.minimumReleaseAge below.

constraints.npm makes Renovate write package-lock.json with npm 11: the major Node 24 bundles, and the one CI's `npm ci` reads it with. npm 12 defaults allow-remote to none, and under --package-lock-only it opens a package that declares bundleDependencies by fetching its tarball URL, which that default refuses (npm/cli#9800). Here that is @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi, so every lockfile update fails, with or without a version change (reproduced on npm 12.2.0), and PR #28 carried package.json alone. Move this with .nvmrc, as the @types/node cap does, and drop it once npm/cli#9800 is fixed.

customManagers.description: Keep the Playwright container tag in the workflows in lockstep with @playwright/test. The browser binaries inside mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v<X>-noble only match the exact npm version, and the visual baselines are generated inside that container.

Keep the renovate-config-validator pinned in scripts/ci/renovate-config.sh current. That script downloads Renovate with npx rather than installing it — the package is ~350 MB, for one path-filtered job — so the version sits outside package-lock.json and nothing else here would ever bump it. The script is in that job's path filter, so that the bump's own pull request runs it. Unpinned it would be whatever the registry served that minute, which is exactly the supply-chain hold minimumReleaseAge exists to prevent.

packageRules.description: TypeScript is capped below 7. The 7.x Go port breaks `next build`, @typescript-eslint and the tsserver `next` plugin. Revisit once eslint-config-next and typescript-eslint both ship a 7-compatible release.
@types/node is capped below 25 so it stays aligned with the Node 24 runtime pinned in .nvmrc and engines.node. Bump the cap together with .nvmrc.

ESLint is capped below 10: eslint-config-next 16 peers `eslint >=9` and the v10 flat-config changes have not been validated against eslint-plugin-security 3. Revisit when eslint-config-next declares v10 support.
Prisma is pinned to 7.x across prisma, @prisma/client and @prisma/adapter-pg — the three must move together, and the 8.x line is still release-candidate only.
next-auth stays on the v5 beta tag until v5 goes stable; the v4 line is a different API.
eslint-config-next must always equal the exact next version, and React must stay below 19.3 for @react-three/fiber 9. One PR for the four.
React is capped below 19.3: @react-three/fiber 9 has not been validated against it.
The three.js stack is version-coupled: drei and fiber pin narrow `three` peer ranges and @types/three tracks three's minor. One PR for all of them.
vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 must be the exact same version or coverage silently reports nothing.
@playwright/test moves together with the container tag matched by customManagers above.
The content-collections packages are versioned independently but released together; a partial bump breaks the build-time MDX pipeline.

argparse is an override, not a dependency: "js-yaml@^3": { "argparse": "^2.0.1" } exists only to drop sprintf-js (GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c) by reusing the 2.0.1 copy js-yaml@4 already installs. A v3 override would add a second argparse version and put an untested major under js-yaml@3. See audit-ci-allowlist.md.

undici is an override, not a dependency: "jsdom": { "undici": "8.12.2" } pins jsdom's copy at the lowest release that clears GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685, GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472 and GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c, because the newest release jsdom's ^8.9.0 admits (8.12.3) was inside the hold on 2026-10-24. jsdom declares ^8, so a v9 override would put an untested major under it. The pin can go once 8.12.3 has aged through the hold. See audit-ci-allowlist.md.

express is an override, not a dependency: "express@^4": "4.22.3" moves the one express@4 node (@lhci/cli's ^4.17.1 and express-rate-limit's peer >=4.11) to the first 4.x whose range reaches qs 6.16 (~6.16.0), which npm update does not do for a node two parents share. The ranged key leaves the MCP SDK's express@5 alone, and a v5 override would hand LHCI a major it never declared. See audit-ci-allowlist.md.

qs is an override, not a dependency: "qs": "6.16.1" pins every copy at the lowest release that clears GHSA-6pq8-jhm2-2vcw (and the two older qs ids), because the newest release the parents' ranges admit (6.16.2) was inside the hold on 2026-11-02. express@4.22.3 and body-parser@1.20.9 declare ~6.16.0, so a 6.17 override would put an untested minor under both. The pin can go once 6.16.2 has aged through the hold. See audit-ci-allowlist.md.

systeminformation is an override, not a dependency: "systeminformation": "5.33.16" pins @dotenvx/dotenvx's copy (under shadcn) at the lowest release that clears GHSA-3f7j-7jwc-fxfj and GHSA-7648-jmwf-vw7j, because the newest release dotenvx's ^5.22.11 admits (5.33.19) was inside the hold on 2026-11-02. A v6 override would put an untested major (still beta) under dotenvx. The pin can go once 5.33.19 has aged through the hold. See audit-ci-allowlist.md.

@hono/node-server is an override, not a dependency: "@hono/node-server": "2.1.3" pins the MCP SDK's copy (under shadcn) at the lowest release that clears GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f, because the newest release the SDK's ^1.19.9 || ^2.0.5 admits (2.1.6) was published on 2026-11-02. A v3 override would put an untested major under the SDK. The pin can go once 2.1.6 has aged through the hold. See audit-ci-allowlist.md.
Type definitions are low risk — automerge them on a branch.
Patch updates are automerged on a branch; CI is the gate.
